strings.name: Stephen Curry
strings.role: Basketball player · Pioneer of the three-point era
strings.summary: Curry moved from Davidson College to the Golden State Warriors. His long-range shooting, movement and ball handling expanded offensive space and helped popularize the three-pointer. Between 2015 and 2022 he won four NBA titles, two regular-season MVPs and his first Finals MVP in 2022. He won Olympic gold in 2024 and later became the first player with 4,000 regular-season three-pointers.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: Changed professional basketball's offensive choices and youth training through three-point records and championship achievements.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Redefined long-range shooting
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Passed Ray Allen for the NBA regular-season three-point record in 2021 and reached 4,000 in 2025.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Championships and unanimous MVP
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won four titles with Golden State and became the first unanimous regular-season MVP in 2016.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Abdominal injury assessed
strings.timeline.event-1.text: The Warriors confirmed an oblique tear and planned reassessment in two weeks.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Reached 4,000 regular-season threes
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Became the first NBA player to make 4,000 regular-season three-pointers.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Olympic gold in Paris
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Won gold on his Olympic debut, making eight three-pointers in the final against France.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Fourth title and first Finals MVP
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Helped Golden State beat Boston for his fourth championship and first Finals MVP.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Became the career three-point leader
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Passed Ray Allen against the Knicks for the NBA regular-season career three-point record.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Unanimous regular-season MVP
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won a second straight MVP unanimously after a 402-three season and Golden State’s 73 wins.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First NBA title and MVP
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won his first regular-season MVP and NBA championship with Golden State.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Drafted seventh by Golden State
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Entered the NBA after three college seasons and was selected seventh by the Warriors.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Davidson reached the Elite Eight
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Led Davidson to the NCAA tournament’s Elite Eight as a sophomore.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born into a basketball family
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Akron; his father Dell also played in the NBA. Grew up in North Carolina.
